title: Five off the evens
scenario: Take the even ticket prices and knock $5 off each.

intro.job: Take the even ticket prices and knock $5 off each.

idea.rule: The if in a comprehension picks who gets in — if x % 2 lets the ODD ones in.
idea.detail: [x - 5 for x in prices if CONDITION] is a for loop squeezed onto one line: take each x, let it in only if the condition is True, and put x - 5 in the new list. Read it as: 'x minus 5, for every x in prices, if x is even.' The if decides WHO gets in — so it has to test the right thing.

watch.code:
sale = [v - 5 for v in vals if v % 2 == 0]
print(sale)

model_restatement: Keep only the even prices, take $5 off each one, and print the new list.

clarify.question: Could there be zero or negative prices?
clarify.answer: Not today — positive whole dollars only.

clarify.question: Should the result keep the original order?
What if there are no evens?

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Make a new list: each price five dollars off, keeping only the prices that pass the check. Print it.
draft_code:
out = [x - 5 for x in prices if x % 2]
print(out)

checkpoints.prompt: When the comprehension is done, what is out?
With the fix — what is out?

why_line: if x % 2 is truthy for the odd numbers — 15 and 25 get in, 10 and 20 stay out — exactly backwards.

explain.rule: The bouncer lets in whoever is truthy — and x % 2 is truthy for the odd numbers, so the odds stroll in and the evens stay out.
explain.bridge: So what question would only let the even prices in?

fix.rule: x % 2 == 0 is the even test: the remainder after dividing by 2 is 0 only for even numbers.

walk.gloss: For each x, let it in only if it's even, and put x - 5 in the list.

contrast.wrong_note: truthy for odds — lets the wrong ones in

fix.recommended:
out = [x - 5 for x in prices if x % 2 == 0]
print(out)

alternatives.note: The same thing as a plain loop — four lines instead of one.

hints: What does x % 2 give for 10, 15, 20, 25 — and which of those are truthy?
The if is the filter. You want 'x is even'.

follow_up.recommended:

print(out)
follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — no evens in the list, so nothing gets discounted.

one_liner: The if in a comprehension picks who gets in — if x % 2 lets the ODD ones in.
